question: How many institutions from how many countries are involved in an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master?
answer: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are prestigious international masters, jointly designed and delivered by a group of higher education institutions. They involve at least 3 institutions from at least 3 different countries, and multiple associated partners from the academic and non-academic world. You will gain either a joint degree (i.e. one single degree certificate issued on behalf of at least two higher education institutions) or multiple degrees (i.e. at least two degree certificates issued by two higher education institutions of the consortium). You’ll be able to define these in detail when you sign a study agreement with the relevant Erasmus Mundus Joint Master at the beginning of your studies. Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (students).

The France Excellence Eiffel scholarship program is a tool developed by the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs to assist French institutions of higher education in attracting the best foreign students to Master's and Doctoral/Phd degree programs. The two main disciplinary fields for the France Excellence Eiffel scholarships cover the following seven areas of study for the Master's and Doctorate elements: For Science and Technology. Presentation of the France Excellence Eiffel Scholarship. French higher education institutions who submit candidates to the France Excellence Eiffel program agree to enroll them: in courses leading to a master's degree in an engineering program in a joint doctoral program (joint supervision of dissertation and/or dual degree), in partnership with a partner institution abroad.

question: What levels of study do Manaaki New Zealand Scholarships cover?
answer: Welcome to the home of Manaaki New Zealand scholarships. Manaaki New Zealand Scholarships help build prosperity, security, and sustainable growth in partner countries and fosters a lifetime connection to Aotearoa New Zealand and the leaders of tomorrow. Recipients of a Manaaki New Zealand Scholarship build life-long connections to each other and to Aotearoa New Zealand while gaining a globally recognised education, an authentically New Zealand experience, and the tools to help their countries achieve the futures they deserve. The Manaaki New Zealand Scholarship Programme aims to enhance the mana of partner countries and Aotearoa New Zealand through manaakitanga - the act of hosting, supporting and honouring manaaki scholars. A Manaaki New Zealand scholarship will change and enrich your life.

question: What does the Manaaki New Zealand Scholarship Programme aim to build in partner countries?
answer: The Manaaki New Zealand Scholarship Programme aims to enhance the mana of partner countries and Aotearoa New Zealand through manaakitanga - the act of hosting, supporting and honouring manaaki scholars. Manaaki New Zealand Scholarships help build prosperity, security, and sustainable growth in partner countries and fosters a lifetime connection to Aotearoa New Zealand and the leaders of tomorrow. Recipients of a Manaaki New Zealand Scholarship build life-long connections to each other and to Aotearoa New Zealand while gaining a globally recognised education, an authentically New Zealand experience, and the tools to help their countries achieve the futures they deserve. Welcome to the home of Manaaki New Zealand scholarships. A Manaaki New Zealand scholarship will change and enrich your life.

question: How many types of MEXT scholarship are there?
answer: As seen in the chart below, there are seven types of the Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho) Scholarship program. Please check with the Japanese embassy or other Japanese diplomatic mission in your country to see if there are any openings in the type and field you wish to apply for. There are two ways to apply for a Japanese Government Scholarship: by applying to the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT) with a recommendation from a Japanese embassy or other Japanese diplomatic mission in your country, or by applying to the MEXT with a recommendation from a Japanese university. In this type of scholarship, scholarship recipients are recruited and initially screened by a Japanese embassy (or consulate general, depending on the country). In addition, the scholarship period and eligibility may vary depending on the type of recommendation framework a university has, so please check with the university you wish to enroll in for details.
